findings.title: Async legacy writes derive context from the request context and get canceled when the request finishes
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines create their timeout context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)` directly from the incoming request `ctx`. Because these methods return immediately after `d.Storage` completes, the HTTP request handler will finish and cancel the request `ctx`, which immediately cancels the derived context in the goroutine and aborts in-flight `d.Legacy` writes with `context.Canceled`. Detach cancellation first with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying `context.WithTimeoutCause`.

findings.title: Wrong duration metrics and high-cardinality `kind` label recorded in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`
findings.body:
Several metric calls in `DualWriterMode3` record to the wrong metric or pass the wrong label value:
- In `Create` (line 45) and `Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(...)`.
- In `DeleteCollection` (line 166), the async goroutine for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` calls `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`.
- In `Delete` (line 106), `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` instead of `options.Kind`, corrupting the `kind` label and introducing unbounded label cardinality in Prometheus.

findings.title: `Delete` passes `d.Log` instead of enriched `log` to context and async legacy errors are not logged
findings.body: In `Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, discarding the added fields. In addition, errors returned by `d.Legacy.Create` (line 55), `d.Legacy.Delete` (line 112), `d.Legacy.Update` (line 139), and `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` (line 165) in the background goroutines are no longer logged, so legacy write failures will fail silently.

findings.title: Mode 3 write tests share a single `mock.Mock` across goroutines and never verify async legacy writes
findings.body:
In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance and the tests return without waiting for the background `Legacy` goroutine:
- The background goroutine calls `m.Called(...)` concurrently with the test goroutine finishing or starting the next subtest, which is a data race on `mock.Mock` state and the shared Prometheus registry `p`.
- In `TestMode3_Create` (lines 40-42), the test case `"error when creating object in the unified store fails"` configures `setupLegacyFn` instead of `setupStorageFn`, which only passes because `ls` and `us` share `m`.
- None of the tests assert that the asynchronous `Legacy` methods were actually called (`TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` do not set up legacy expectations at all).
